content.title: About
content.content: Asparagus is the young shoot of the herbaceous plant Asparagus officinalis. Raw green asparagus has a delicate, slightly nutty flavor and a crisp texture. It is rich in vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber while being low in calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus is one of the oldest cultivated vegetables, with a history of over 2,000 years.
In ancient Rome, asparagus was served only to the emperor and the elite.
There are three main varieties: green, white (grown in darkness), and purple.
The fresh asparagus season in the Northern Hemisphere runs from April to June.
Raw asparagus contains more than 200 compounds, including antioxidants such as glutathione.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate supports cell division and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 kcal, making asparagus an excellent choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Asparagus provides glutathione, vitamin C, and beta‑carotene, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to asparagus, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Asparagus contains oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Raw asparagus should be thoroughly washed to remove possible contaminants and bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw asparagus can be thinly sliced into salads, added to smoothies, used in rolls, or enjoyed as a crunchy side. It can also be lightly marinated in lemon juice and olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store asparagus in the refrigerator wrapped in a slightly damp cloth or placed in a perforated bag in the vegetable drawer. Use within 3–5 days. Discard if it develops a yellowish coating or becomes limp.
